title: Hardware Isolation and Fault Containment
summary: Work through Hardware Isolation and Fault Containment.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Hardware Isolation and Fault Containment** in *The Nervous System* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, The Nervous System, § Hardware Isolation and Fault Containment
blocks.md: A large current transient during a neural accelerator burst can pull down a shared power rail and brown out or reset the permission processor without warning, while memory bus contention on a shared interconnect can delay safety checks past the hard real-time execution tick. Even when safety enforcement executes on a dedicated processor, physical coupling to the proposal engine can silently undermine software isolation.

questions.q: The section **Hardware Isolation and Fault Containment** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Under any workload the proposer can generate, the permission path must meet its response bound and keep its authority to refuse, and separate processors are one realization of that requirement, a hypothesis that loaded tests must still confirm.

An admitted chunk may drive the actuators only for a lease counted on the permission path's own clock, derived from the plant: longer than the renewal period plus jitter and short enough to fit under the pre-brake ceiling of the stopping budget.

Sample-and-hold, compute, and bus transport each subtract omega_c*tau of phase at crossover, so fast loops must close inside the drive and the permission tick can supervise them but never sit in them.

Each tier takes its rate from a different physical constant (winding L/R and the PWM carrier for the current loop, base travel per tick for the permission tick, weight-sweep cost for the chunk policy, prefill cost for the intent model), not from convenience.
